value: threshold in the range of 1 m/s2 (printed 'ms2'), minimum at 1,000 Hz
method: extracellular hook-electrode recordings from the midleg main leg nerve (carrying the femoral chordotonal and subgenual organ axons) of restrained females, tibia glued to a lever; sinusoidal substrate vibration from a Bruel and Kjaer 4810 minishaker (100 ms, 2/s, six 6 dB amplitude steps, carriers 200 to 8,000 Hz), acceleration measured with an accelerometer
conditions: adult females caught in open aspen forest around the Biological Station of the University of Michigan (Pellston, MI) in July 2013 and June 2017, kept in cages with fresh aspen or acer branches and used within 2 or 3 d; recording temperature not stated; substrate vibration only (no airborne sound); responses from 13 animals analysed; the threshold curve (Fig. 3B) is the mean and SEM of the 13 animals, and the text gives no per-frequency threshold numbers or per-frequency n; animal fixed ventral side up with wax-collophonium and dissected ventrally; threshold analysed as all-or-nothing, the lowest intensity giving a response to at least three of four stimuli per frequency and amplitude; the Results also print that the overall threshold is broadly tuned to vibrations from 200 to 5,000 Hz; latency fell from about 13-17 ms at threshold to 5-7 ms at larger accelerations with large variation (separate paragraph); no sex comparison (females only); the Abstract adds that no tuning to the peak frequency of the calling song (9 kHz) could be found, and the Discussion reports a decrease of sensitivity at higher frequency

source.title: Sensing of Substrate Vibrations in the Adult Cicada Okanagana rimosa (Hemiptera: Cicadidae)

note: Page body prints no licence sentence; Crossref lists CC BY-NC 4.0 (content-version vor). Name Okanagana rimosa (Say, 1830), Cicadidae, Hemiptera: included as a valid species (type species of Okanagana, subspecies rimosa rimosa and rimosa ohioensis) in the Okanagana treatment of Cole et al. 2023, Zootaxa 5346(5): 501-531 (Plazi); ITIS TSN 847181 places it in Hemiptera, Cicadoidea, Tibicininae; the paper names no subspecies (audit 367). Unit typo 'ms2' is the article's; the abstract prints 'about 1 m/s2'. Not a repeat: Okanagana rimosa appears on main only as host in Emblemasoma auditrix (d229).
